//! Owner-mediated release publication in the running HTTP process.
use super::*;
use crate::release_control::Command;
#[cfg(unix)]
use crate::release_control::Listener;
use snapback4_core::engine::release::ReleaseActivation;

#[cfg(unix)]
pub(super) fn start(
    shared: Arc<Shared>,
    dir: std::path::PathBuf,
) -> Result<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>, String> {
    let store = shared
        .owner
        .as_ref()
        .ok_or("release control requires a persisted owner")?
        .path()
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let listener = Listener::bind(&dir, store)?;
    crate::lifecycle::managed_cleanup();
    crate::lifecycle::background("release-control", move || {
        listener.run(|command| apply(&shared, &dir, command))
    })
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#5-hot-activation-and-ownership — only assignments and committed rebind follow the database commit.
pub(super) fn apply(
    shared: &Shared,
    dir: &std::path::Path,
    command: Command,
) -> Result<Json, String> {
    match command {
        Command::Stop => {
            crate::lifecycle::request_stop();
            Ok(json!({"stopping":true}))
        }
        Command::Status {
            after,
            items_after,
            event,
        } => {
            shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
            let mut status=engine.store_mut().release_status(after,items_after.as_deref(),event).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            status["clock"]=json!({"now":shared.now(),"offsetMs":lock(&shared.clock).offset()});
            Ok(status)
            })
        },
        Command::Prune {
            confirm,
            expected_revision,
        } => {
            let mut result = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, _| engine.store_mut().prune_dormant(confirm, Some(expected_revision)))
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if let Some(items) = result["items"].as_array_mut() {
                items.truncate(16);
            }
            result["items_after"] = result["items"]
                .as_array()
                .and_then(|items| items.last())
                .map(|i| i["key"].clone())
                .unwrap_or(Json::Null);
            Ok(result)
        }
        Command::Activate {
            activation_protocol,
            release,
            expected_release,
            expected_revision,
            digest,
            rollback,
            visible_rollback,
            registry_custody,
            restore_dormant,
            allow_feed_adoption,
        } => {
            if activation_protocol != crate::release_control::ACTIVATION_PROTOCOL {
                return Err("release activation protocol differs; restart serve with this CLI before switching releases".into());
            }
            if release == 0 {
                return Err("release id must be positive".into());
            }
            let project = Project {
                root: dir.join("releases").join(release.to_string()),
            };
            if !std::fs::symlink_metadata(&project.root)
                .is_ok_and(|m| m.is_dir() && !m.file_type().is_symlink())
            {
                return Err(format!(
                    "release {release} is not an immutable release directory"
                ));
            }
            if !registry_custody{return Err("release custody requires an updated release-control client; use this runtime's CLI".into())}
            crate::verbs::validate_registered_view(dir,&project.root)?;
            if crate::release_files::digest(&project.root)? != digest {
                return Err("staged release content changed; redeploy its exact source".into());
            }
            if project.sources().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.is_empty() {
                return Err(format!(
                    "release {release} has no Quarry source; select a complete immutable release"
                ));
            }
            let bound = project.compile().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if !bound.diagnostics.is_empty() {
                return Err(bound
                    .diagnostics
                    .iter()
                    .map(ToString::to_string)
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                    .join("\n"));
            }
            let prepared = crate::native::prepare(&project, &bound).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            crate::dev_worker::prepare_release(&project, &bound.schema)?;
            crate::release_files::link_store(&project.root)?;
            if crate::release_files::digest(&project.root)? != digest {
                return Err("release artifacts changed during preparation; retry after inspecting immutable source".into());
            }
            crate::release_files::durable(&project.root)?;
            let mut pointer =
                crate::release_files::Pointer::prepare(dir, release, expected_release, rollback)?;
            let options = ReleaseActivation {
                visibility:crate::verbs::visibility_policy(&project.root)?.or_else(||visible_rollback.then(Default::default)),
                release,
                expected_previous: expected_release,
                expected_revision: Some(expected_revision),
                restore_dormant,
                native_digest: prepared.installed.as_ref().map(|m| m.digest.clone()),
                operation: if rollback { "rollback" } else { "deploy" }.into(),
            };
            let _requests=shared.release_requests.write();
            shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
            lock(&shared.readers).begin_adoption(&bound);
            let generation = match engine.adopt_release_at(
                bound.schema.clone(),
                bound.programs.iter().map(|p| p.program.clone()),
                &options,
                allow_feed_adoption,
                shared.now(),
            ) {
                Ok(generation) => generation,
                Err(error) => {
                    lock(&shared.readers).finish_adoption();
                    return Err(error.to_string());
                }
            };
            #[cfg(test)]
            test_work(&shared.release_committed);
            engine.set_prepared_native(prepared.module);
            engine.set_presence(Some(shared.presence.clone()));
            shared.refresh_time_audience_clock(engine, shared.now());
            lock(&shared.readers).replace(engine, &bound.refusal_sites);
            {
                let mut active = lock(&shared.bound);
                let mut advertised = lock(&shared.generation);
                let mut native = lock(&shared.native);
                shared.latency.adopt(&bound);
                *active = bound;
                *advertised = generation;
                *native = prepared.installed;
                let mut root = lock(&shared.release_root);
                *root = Some(project.root);
                shared.worker_revision.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Release);
            }
            crate::lifecycle::generation(generation);
            shared.publish_engine(engine);
            // Completion I/O can fail, but never abandons the new runtime.
            pointer.finish(generation)?;
            snapback4_core::diagnostic!(
                "snapback4 serve: release {release} activated without restart as generation {generation}"
            );
            Ok(
                json!({"release":release,"generation":generation,"revision":expected_revision+1,"hot":true,"adoption":engine.store().adoption_report().compact(),"details":engine.store().adoption_report().summary(),"backfills":engine.store().adoption_report().backfills}),
            )
            })
        }
    }
}

//! Release checks at the activation transaction's snapshot.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#5-hot-activation-and-ownership — retain the selected-release check before the revision check.
use crate::{
    RuntimeError,
    engine::release::ReleaseTransaction,
};
use rusqlite::{Connection, OptionalExtension};

/// Borrowed before activation constructs its row-access transaction.
pub(crate) struct ReleaseCheck<'a>(pub(super) &'a Connection);

impl<'store> From<&ReleaseCheck<'store>> for crate::store_port::AnyPreparation<'store, '_> {
    fn from(check: &ReleaseCheck<'store>) -> Self {
        Self::Sqlite(ReleaseCheck(check.0))
    }
}

impl ReleaseTransaction for ReleaseCheck<'_> {
    fn selected_release(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(self
            .0
            .query_row("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='release'", [], |r| {
                r.get(0)
            })
            .optional()?)
    }
    fn release_revision(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(self
            .0
            .query_row(
                "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='release_revision'",
                [],
                |r| r.get(0),
            )
            .optional()?)
    }
}

impl ReleaseTransaction for super::Tx<'_> {
    fn selected_release(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> { self.meta("release") }
    fn release_revision(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> { self.meta("release_revision") }
}

//! Development doors beside the operation routes: `POST /seed`, `POST /dev/reset`, and the
//! `--no-watch` hint that names a schema edited on disk after adoption.
use super::{Shared, lock, refusal_json, respond_timed};
use crate::project::{Project, SourceStamp};
use serde_json::{Value as Json, json};
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use snapback4_core::wire;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Mutex;
use tiny_http::Request;

/// The source stamp each `--no-watch` dev host adopted, by project root.
static PINNED: Mutex<BTreeMap<PathBuf, SourceStamp>> = Mutex::new(BTreeMap::new());

pub(super) fn closed() -> Refusal {
    Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "development doors are closed; use serve staging with real users (guide staging), or explicitly opt into dev --unsafe-dev-doors for local fixtures").guide("staging")
}

pub(super) fn pin(project: &Path, stamp: SourceStamp) {
    PINNED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).insert(project.to_owned(), stamp);
}

/// A `--no-watch` host serves the schema it started with. When a request
/// names an operation or argument that host does not know and the `.q` files
/// changed on disk since, say so: the edit is real, it was just never adopted.
pub(super) fn stale(shared: &Shared, refusal: Refusal) -> Refusal {
    let Some(adopted) = PINNED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).get(&shared.project).copied() else { return refusal };
    if (Project { root: shared.project.clone() }).sources_stamp() == adopted { return refusal; }
    let message = format!("{}; this dev host runs with --no-watch and snapback/ changed on disk after it adopted its schema, so the edit is not served", refusal.message);
    Refusal { message, rewrite: Some("restart `snapback4 dev` (or drop --no-watch so saves re-adopt), then retry".into()), ..refusal }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#8 — persona names are not their principals; dev only.
pub(super) fn persona_argument(shared: &Shared, kinds: &BTreeMap<String,snapback4_core::ir::ArgType>, args: &Json) -> Option<Refusal> {
    if !shared.personas { return None; }
    let bound = lock(&shared.bound);
    crate::persona_principals::arguments(&bound.personas,kinds,args)
}
// Rows are written as the system principal; each names its id because seed is an upsert by id.
pub(super) fn seed(request: Request, shared: &Shared, body: &str) {
    if !shared.dev_doors() || !request.remote_addr().is_some_and(|a| a.ip().is_loopback()) {
        respond_timed(request, shared, 403, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "seeding is a development door")) }));
        return;
    }
    let refuse = |request, refusal: Refusal| respond_timed(request, shared, 400, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&refusal.guide("personas")) }));
    let rows: Vec<Json> = match serde_json::from_str(body) {
        Ok(Json::Array(rows)) => rows,
        _ => return refuse(request, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "seed takes a JSON array of {table, row}")),
    };
    let outcome = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
        shared.dev_authority(engine).map_err(|why| (403, why))?;
        let now = shared.now();
        let typed = typed_rows(engine.schema(), &rows, now).map_err(|why| (400, why.guide("personas")))?;
        let count = engine.seed_at(typed, now).map_err(|error| (200, seed_refusal(error)))?;
        shared.durable_committed(engine);
        Ok::<_, (u16, Refusal)>(count)
    });
    match outcome {
        Ok(count) => respond_timed(request, shared, 200, json!({"seeded":count})),
        Err((status, why)) => respond_timed(request, shared, status, json!({"denied":why})),
    }

}

/// `/seed` rows checked against the served schema and typed, or the first problem.
fn typed_rows(schema: &snapback4_core::Schema, rows: &[Json], now: i64) -> Result<Vec<(String, snapback4_core::Value)>, Refusal> {
    let mut typed = Vec::new();
    for (index, entry) in rows.iter().enumerate() {
        let (Some(table), Some(row)) = (entry.get("table").and_then(Json::as_str), entry.get("row")) else {
            return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "each seed entry is {table, row}"));
        };
        let Some(definition) = schema.table(table) else {
            return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("unknown table {table}")));
        };
        if row.is_object() && row.get("id").is_none_or(|id| !id.is_string()) {
            return Err(missing_id(index, table));
        }
        let mut row = row.clone();
        crate::verbs::test_fixture::relative_times(definition, &mut row, now)
            .map_err(|why| Refusal::new("E_FIXTURE_TIME", "input", format!("seed row {index} ({table}): {why}")))?;
        if let Some(why) = wire::bare_principal(definition, &row) {
            return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("seed row {index} ({table}): {why}")));
        }
        match wire::row_from_json(definition, &row) {
            Ok(value) => typed.push((table.to_owned(), value)),
            Err(why) => return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("{table}: {why}"))),
        }
    }
    Ok(typed)
}

fn seed_refusal(error: snapback4_core::RuntimeError) -> Refusal {
    let mut refusal = error.refusal();
    // Reseeding with changed immutable values reads like a rule problem; say what happened.
    if refusal.code == "E_CONSTRAINT" && refusal.message.ends_with(" is immutable") {
        refusal.message.push_str("; /seed is an upsert by id, and a row with that id already exists with a different value in that column. Reseed it with its original value, give the row a new id, POST /dev/reset first, or restart dev with --memory for an empty store");
    }
    refusal
}

/// What `POST /dev/reset` was asked to do: the body is empty, a `/seed`
/// array, or `{"seed": [..], "clock": "reset"}` with either key optional.
#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
struct ResetRequest { seed: Vec<Json>, clock: bool }

fn reset_request(body: &str) -> Result<ResetRequest, Refusal> {
    const SHAPE: &str = "reset takes no body, a /seed array [{table, row}, ..], or {\"seed\": [..], \"clock\": \"reset\"} with either key optional";
    if body.trim().is_empty() { return Ok(ResetRequest::default()); }
    match serde_json::from_str(body) {
        Ok(Json::Array(seed)) => Ok(ResetRequest { seed, clock: false }),
        Ok(Json::Object(fields)) => {
            let mut request = ResetRequest::default();
            for (key, value) in fields {
                match (key.as_str(), value) {
                    ("seed", Json::Array(seed)) => request.seed = seed,
                    ("clock", Json::String(clock)) if clock == "reset" => request.clock = true,
                    ("clock", Json::String(clock)) if clock == "keep" => request.clock = false,
                    ("clock", other) => return Err(crate::dev_clock::input(format!("reset's clock is \"reset\" (back to wall time) or \"keep\" (the default), not {other}"))),
                    (key, _) => return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("{SHAPE}; got key {key:?}"))),
                }
            }
            Ok(request)
        }
        _ => Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", SHAPE)),
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.25 — one transaction: empty, new identity, reseed; then the host's caches follow.
pub(super) fn reset(request: Request, shared: &Shared, body: &str) {
    if !shared.dev_doors() || !request.remote_addr().is_some_and(|a| a.ip().is_loopback()) {
        respond_timed(request, shared, 403, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&reset_release()) }));
        return;
    }
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    let refuse = |request, refusal: Refusal| respond_timed(request, shared, 400, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&refusal.guide("testing")) }));
    let asked = match reset_request(body) {
        Ok(asked) => asked,
        Err(refusal) => return refuse(request, refusal),
    };
    // Serialize with clock advances, then take the engine before the clock:
    // the order clock advance and worker claims use.
    let advance = lock(&shared.maintenance).advance.clone();
    let _advance = lock(&advance);
    let result = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {

    shared.dev_authority(engine).map_err(|why| (403, why))?;
    let mut clock = lock(&shared.clock).clone();
    if asked.clock { clock.reset().map_err(|why| (400, why))?; }
    let now = clock.now();
    // Resolve against the prospective reset clock before changing any durable state.
    let typed = typed_rows(engine.schema(), &asked.seed, now).map_err(|why| (400, why))?;
    let reset = engine.dev_reset_at(typed, now).map_err(|error| (200, seed_refusal(error)))?;
    if asked.clock { *lock(&shared.clock) = clock; }
    *lock(&shared.dev_reset_store) = Some(reset.store_id.clone());
    // The reset committed a new identity and a new authority clock. Replace,
    // rather than max with, the retired store's cached high-water mark.
    shared.time_audience_clock.store(if engine.schema().tables.values().any(|t| t.not_before.is_some()) { now } else { i64::MIN }, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
    // Detached readers reopen; the following registry, change answers and
    // `/dev/status` forget the old identity. Wake then names the new store,
    // so every held poll returns and each client sees the replacement.
    let sites = lock(&shared.bound).refusal_sites.clone();
    lock(&shared.readers).replace(engine, &sites);
    lock(&shared.adoption).store_id = reset.store_id.clone();
    if let Ok(reader) = snapback4_core::engine::following_history::Reader::new() { *lock(&shared.following) = reader; }
    *lock(&shared.change_answers) = Default::default();
    shared.durable_committed(engine);
    let generation = engine.generation();
    Ok::<_, (u16, Refusal)>((reset, generation))
    });
    let (reset, generation) = match result {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err((status, why)) => return respond_timed(request, shared, status, json!({"denied":why})),
    };
    let assets = reset.assets.len();
    if let Err(error) = reset.assets.remove_files() { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4 dev: reset left asset bytes behind: {error}"); }
    let now = shared.now();
    snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4 dev: store reset (store {} → {}, seeded {}) in {} ms", reset.previous_store_id, reset.store_id, reset.seeded, started.elapsed().as_millis());
    respond_timed(request, shared, 200, json!({
        "sessionNotice":"Reset replaced the store and removed its accounts and sessions. Discard cached credentials/localStorage for this backend, sign up again and reprovision roles; use a fresh memory host per independent proof.",
        "reset": true, "seeded": reset.seeded, "generation": generation, "storeId": reset.store_id,
        "previousStoreId": reset.previous_store_id, "head": reset.seq, "assetsRemoved": assets,
        "now": now, "clockOffsetMs": lock(&shared.clock).offset(), "skewMs": now - snapback4_core::now_ms(), "ms": started.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,
    }));
}

pub(super) fn reset_release() -> Refusal {
    Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "resetting the store is a development door; snapback4 serve never empties a store")
        .guide("testing")
}

fn missing_id(index: usize, table: &str) -> Refusal {
    Refusal::new("E_FIELD", "input", format!(
        "missing field id: seed row {index} ({table}) has no string id. /seed is an upsert by id, so every row names its own; \
         rerunning the same seed then updates those rows instead of duplicating them"))
        .rewrite("give each row a 26-character id in Crockford base32 (digits and capital letters except I, L, O, U), \
                  e.g. \"row\": {\"id\": \"0000000000000000000000SEED\", ..}; in JavaScript `idFrom(\"seed:alice\")` from \
                  snapback4/client derives the same valid id from a label every time, and a reference column takes that id")
}

        assert!(snapback4_core::ids::minted_at(example).is_some(), "{example} is Crockford base32");

    }
}

//! A process-local clock for development and explicitly classified staging stores.
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — preserve expiry tests and tell callers how to recover.
pub(crate) const SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Time travel also advances session expiry and unplaced-upload collection: seven-day password sessions may now be expired. Sign in again after the jump and upload unplaced bytes after it; never replay an ambiguous clock advance.";

pub(crate) const PRESERVED_SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Authenticated development and staging sessions keep their remaining lifetime across this jump; sessions:expire explicitly tests credential expiry. Unplaced uploads still age. Never replay an ambiguous advance.";

const MAX_TIME: i64 = snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX;

pub fn input(message: impl Into<String>) -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INPUT", "clock", message).guide("clock") }
pub fn release() -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY", "clock", "clock controls require dev or a deploy --staging store; production always uses wall time").guide("clock") }

/// Isolated time tests stay inside an assigned range, or request a free port.
pub(crate) fn isolated_command() -> String {
    isolated_range(std::env::var("PORT_LO").ok().as_deref(), std::env::var("PORT_HI").ok().as_deref())
}
fn isolated_range(lo: Option<&str>, hi: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match (lo.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok()), hi.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())) {
        (Some(lo), Some(hi)) if lo > 0 && hi >= lo => format!("dev --memory --port {lo}-{hi} within the current range"),
        _ => "dev --memory --port 0".into(),
    }
}

pub fn duration(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if text.starts_with('-') { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
    let text = text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text);
    let split = text.bytes().position(|b| !b.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(text.len());
    let (number, unit) = text.split_at(split);
    let multiplier = match unit { "ms" => 1, "s" => 1_000, "m" => 60_000, "h" => 3_600_000, "d" => 86_400_000, "w" => 604_800_000, _ => 0 };
    number.parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(multiplier)).filter(|n| *n > 0 && *n <= MAX_TIME)
        .ok_or_else(|| input("expected a positive whole duration with ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as +25h"))
}

pub fn offset(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if let Some(rest) = text.strip_prefix('-') { duration(rest).map(|n| -n) } else { duration(text) }
}

fn time(value: Option<i64>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    value.filter(|n| (0..=MAX_TIME).contains(n)).ok_or_else(|| input("time must be Unix milliseconds in 0..9007199254740991; choose a smaller time or duration"))
}

pub fn run_now(text: Option<&String>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    let now = snapback4_core::now_ms();
    match text {
        None => Ok(now),
        Some(text) if text.starts_with('+') => time(now.checked_add(duration(text)?)),
        Some(text) => time(text.parse().ok()),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Clock {
    dev: bool,
    base: i64,
    offset: i64,
    started: Instant,
    epoch: String,
    revision: u64,
    #[cfg(test)]
    frozen: bool,
}

impl Clock {
    pub fn new(dev: bool, offset: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        if !dev && offset != 0 { return Err(release()); }
        Ok(Self { dev, offset, base: time(snapback4_core::now_ms().checked_add(offset))?, started: Instant::now(),
            epoch: snapback4_core::ids::mint(snapback4_core::now_ms(), &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?, revision: 0, #[cfg(test)] frozen: false })
    }
    pub fn staging(offset: i64, floor: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        let mut clock = Self::new(true, offset)?;
        let delta = floor.saturating_sub(clock.now()).max(0);
        if delta > 0 { clock.advance(delta)?; }
        Ok(clock)
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn freeze(&mut self, now: i64) { self.base = now; self.frozen = true; }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        #[cfg(test)] if self.frozen { return self.base; }
        if !self.dev { return snapback4_core::now_ms(); }
        self.base.saturating_add(self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64).min(MAX_TIME)
    }
    /// Identifies samples taken before/after a restart or deliberate clock jump.
    pub fn offset(&self) -> i64 { self.offset }
    pub fn revision(&self) -> String { format!("{}:{}", self.epoch, self.revision) }
    pub fn presence_now(&self) -> i64 {
        // Production grace is elapsed real time, unaffected by wall-clock corrections.
        if self.dev { self.now() } else { self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64 }
    }
    /// Back to wall time: the offset `--clock-offset` and every advance added
    /// is dropped (a development reset's `{"clock":"reset"}`).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = 0;
        self.base = snapback4_core::now_ms();
        self.started = Instant::now();
        #[cfg(test)] { self.frozen = false; }
        Ok(self.base)
    }
    pub fn advance(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        if milliseconds <= 0 { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
        let next = time(self.now().checked_add(milliseconds))?;
        let offset = self.offset.checked_add(milliseconds).ok_or_else(|| input("cumulative clock offset overflow"))?;
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = offset;
        self.base = next;
        self.started = Instant::now();
        Ok(next)
    }
}

/// The control CLI only talks to a loopback dev host. It does not open its store.
pub fn command(options: &crate::verbs::Options) -> i32 {
    let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
        let draining = options.positionals == ["drain"];
        if !draining && (options.positionals.len() != 2 || options.positionals[0] != "advance") {
            return Err(input(format!("usage: {}", crate::cli_flags::synopsis("clock"))).to_string());
        }
        let duration_text = if draining { "0ms" } else { options.positionals[1].as_str() };
        if !draining { duration(duration_text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; }
        let release_path = options.flags.get("release").map(|dir| std::path::PathBuf::from(dir).join("store.sqlite"));
        if release_path.is_some() && options.flags.contains_key("port") { return Err("clock --release does not accept --port".into()); }
        let (address, instance, token) = if let Some(path) = &release_path {
            let store = snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::open_read_only(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if store.deployment_environment().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(release().to_string()); }
            let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(path).ok_or("staging clock requires a running serve")?;
            let session = crate::serve::token::mint_live(path, "clock", 1).map_err(|(_,error)|error)?;
            (address,None,Some(session.token))
        } else {
            let (address,instance)=crate::verbs::dev_address(options)?;
            // A production listener has no development-token registry entry.
            // Ask its read-only clock door first so the CLI preserves the
            // server's actionable refusal instead of failing token discovery.
            if let Ok((_, status)) = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/clock/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5))
                && status["denied"]["code"] == "E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY"
            {
                return Err(release().to_string());
            }
            let token=crate::verbs::mint_for_dev(address,"operator",1)?;
            (address,instance,Some(token))
        };
        let mut body = serde_json::json!({"duration":duration_text,"eachBoundary":options.flags.contains_key("each-boundary"), "drain":!options.flags.contains_key("no-drain"), "allowHeld":options.flags.contains_key("allow-held")});
        if options.flags.contains_key("expire-sessions") { body["sessions"] = "expire".into(); }
        if draining && options.flags.contains_key("no-drain") { return Err(input("clock drain does not accept --no-drain").to_string()); }
        let body = body.to_string();
        // The common HTTP/1.0 exchange is EOF-delimited and bounds replies at
        // 64 MiB, enough for the preflight's complete explicit window report.
        let response = if release_path.is_some() {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_authorized(address,"POST","/dev/clock/advance",None,token.as_deref(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        } else {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_dev_authorized(address,"/dev/clock/advance",instance.as_deref(),token.as_deref().unwrap(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        };
        let (status, json) = response.map_err(|error| {
            let evidence = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5)).ok()
                .map(|(_, status)| format!("now={}, skewMs={}", status["now"], status["skewMs"]))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "clock status unavailable".into());
            format!("clock advance reply failed at {address}: {error}; time may already have advanced ({evidence}); inspect /dev/status and queued work before retrying; for an isolated dev pass --port N")
        })?;
        if let Some(notice) = json["sessionNotice"].as_str() { eprintln!("clock: {notice}"); }
        if let Some(held) = json["held"].as_array() {
            for schedule in held.iter().filter(|s| s["holdCode"] == "saved-boundary") {
                eprintln!("clock: schedule {}: {}", schedule["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"), schedule["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or("held"));
            }
        }
        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
            if json.get("now").is_some() {
                eprintln!("clock: incomplete advance report (time already moved): {}", serde_json::json!({"now":json["now"],"fired":json["fired"],"held":json["held"]}));
            }
            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
        }
        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
        Ok(json.to_string())
    })();
    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
}

//! Exact service principals named by compiled authorization facts.
use snapback4_core::{
    Value,
    ir::{BinaryOp, Expr, Input, Stmt},
    schema::{RuleExpr, RuleTerm},
};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

fn principal(value: &Value) -> Option<&str> {
    match value {
        Value::Id(value) => value
            .strip_prefix("service:")
            .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
            .map(|_| value.as_str()),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn rule(rule: &RuleExpr, seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>, positive: bool) {
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Viewer, RuleTerm::Literal(value))
        | RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Literal(value), RuleTerm::Viewer)
            if positive =>
        {
            if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
                seats.insert(value.into());
            }
        }
        RuleExpr::And(rules) | RuleExpr::Or(rules) => rules
            .iter()
            .for_each(|rule| self::rule(rule, seats, positive)),
        RuleExpr::Not(rule) => self::rule(rule, seats, !positive),
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn expression(expr: &Expr, seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>, positive: bool) {
    match expr {
        Expr::Binary {
            op: BinaryOp::Eq | BinaryOp::SameValueZero,
            left,
            right,
        } => match (&**left, &**right, positive) {
            (Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), Expr::Literal(value), true)
            | (Expr::Literal(value), Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), true) => {
                if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
                    seats.insert(value.into());
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        },
        Expr::Binary {
            op: BinaryOp::And | BinaryOp::Or,
            left,
            right,
        } => {
            expression(left, seats, positive);
            expression(right, seats, positive);
        }
        Expr::Unary {
            op: snapback4_core::ir::UnaryOp::Not,
            value,
        } => expression(value, seats, !positive),
        Expr::Block { body, value } => {
            statements(body, seats);
            expression(value, seats, positive);
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn statements(body: &[Stmt], seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {
    for statement in body {
        match statement {
            Stmt::Require { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
            Stmt::If {
                then_body,
                else_body,
                ..
            } => {
                statements(then_body, seats);
                statements(else_body, seats);
            }
            Stmt::For { body, .. } => statements(body, seats),
            Stmt::Check { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
            Stmt::WriteTarget {
                condition: Some(condition),
                ..
            } => statements(&condition.setup, seats),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — minted seats stay ordinary principals; this is advisory schema evidence, never a grant.
pub(crate) fn collect(bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    let mut seats = BTreeSet::new();
    for table in bound.schema.tables.values() {
        for rule in [
            &table.rules.read,
            &table.rules.insert,
            &table.rules.update,
            &table.rules.delete,
        ] {
            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
        }
        for rule in table.column_reads.values() {
            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
        }
    }
    for program in &bound.programs {
        statements(&program.program.body, &mut seats);
    }
    seats.extend(
        bound
            .schema
            .schedules
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|schedule| schedule.service.clone()),
    );
    seats.extend(
        bound
            .schema
            .routes
            .values()
            .filter_map(|route| route.service.clone()),
    );
    seats
}

/** @throws deadline expires; work rejection propagates. */
export async function bounded<T>(work: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  try {
    return await Promise.race([work, new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
      timer = setTimeout(() => reject(Error(`${label} timed out after ${ms} ms`)), ms);
    })]);
  } finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
}
/** Attempts every cleanup, even if a preceding step fails or stalls. */
/** @throws AggregateError after every cleanup was attempted; each step has a 10-second bound. */
export async function cleanup(...steps: Array<(() => unknown | Promise<unknown>) | undefined>): Promise<void> {
  const errors: unknown[] = [];
  for (const step of steps) if (step) {
    try { await bounded(Promise.resolve().then(step), 10_000, "proof cleanup"); }
    catch (error) { errors.push(error); }
  }
  if (errors.length) throw new AggregateError(errors, "proof cleanup failed");
}
/** @throws invalid handle/deadline, host stop failure or TERM/KILL reap deadline. */
export async function stopChild(child: ChildProcess | Pick<ProofHost, "url" | "stop">, graceMs = 5000): Promise<void> {
  deadline(graceMs, 5000);
  if (child && "url" in child && typeof child.url === "string" && typeof child.stop === "function") {
    await bounded(Promise.resolve().then(() => child.stop()), graceMs + 10_000, "host stop"); return;
  }
  if (!child || !("kill" in child) || typeof child.kill !== "function" || typeof child.once !== "function"
      || !(child.exitCode === null || typeof child.exitCode === "number")
      || !(child.signalCode === null || typeof child.signalCode === "string")) {
    throw new TypeError("stopChild needs a ChildProcess or { url, stop }");
  }
  if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) { await groupGone(child); return; }
  let done!: () => void;
  const exited = new Promise<void>(resolve => { done = resolve; });
  child.once("exit", done);
  child.once("error", done);
  try {
    child.kill("SIGTERM");
    try { await bounded(exited, graceMs, "SIGTERM"); }
    catch {
      child.kill("SIGKILL");
      await bounded(exited, 5000, "SIGKILL reap");
    }
  } finally { child.removeListener("exit", done); child.removeListener("error", done); }
  await groupGone(child);
}
async function groupGone(child: ChildProcess): Promise<void> {
  const pid = privateGroups.get(child);
  if (!pid || process.platform === "win32") return;
  const existing = groupClosures.get(child);
  if (existing) return existing;
  const cleanup = (async () => {
    const expires = performance.now() + 5000;
    for (;;) {
      try { process.kill(-pid, 0); }
      catch (error) { if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ESRCH") return; throw error; }
      const remaining = expires - performance.now();
      if (remaining <= 0) throw Error("proof process-group cleanup timed out after 5000 ms");
      await sleep(Math.min(10, remaining));
    }
  })();
  groupClosures.set(child, cleanup);
  return cleanup;
}

export function portRange(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): string {
  const low = env.PORT_LO, high = env.PORT_HI;
  if (low === undefined && high === undefined) return "0";
  if (!low || !high || !/^\d+$/.test(low) || !/^\d+$/.test(high)
      || Number(low) < 1 || Number(high) > 65535 || Number(low) > Number(high)) {
    throw Error("PORT_LO and PORT_HI must both specify an inclusive range, 1 <= low <= high <= 65535");
  }
  return `${Number(low)}-${Number(high)}`;
}

  const logs = { stdout: join(directory, `${id}.stdout.log`), stderr: join(directory, `${id}.stderr.log`) };
  if (options.secret) writeFileSync(logs.stdout, "stdout withheld: secret command (returned only to caller)\n", { flag: "wx", mode: 0o600 });
  const out = options.secret ? undefined : openSync(logs.stdout, "wx", 0o600), err = openSync(logs.stderr, "wx", 0o600);
  const grouped = options.processGroup === true && process.platform !== "win32";
  // Frontends are already detached group leaders with an in-group keeper.
  // Record their group too, so stop/startup cleanup cannot report success
  // before Vite plugins and other inherited descendants have left custody.
  const privateGroup = process.platform !== "win32" && (grouped || options.detached === true);
  const executable = grouped ? process.execPath : command;
  const executableArgs = grouped ? [resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL("./proof-command.js", import.meta.url))), command, ...args] : [...args];
  let child: ChildProcess;
  try { child = spawn(executable, executableArgs, { cwd, detached: grouped || (options.detached ?? false), env: { ...(options.env ?? process.env), SNAPBACK4_PROOF_LAUNCH: id }, stdio: [grouped || options.livenessPipe ? "pipe" : "ignore", options.secret ? "pipe" : out!, err, ...(grouped ? ["ipc" as const] : [])] }); }
  finally { if (out !== undefined) closeSync(out); closeSync(err); }
  if (privateGroup && child.pid) privateGroups.set(child, child.pid);
  // Secret stdout never reaches a file, even briefly. Callers still receive it.
  let stdout = "";
  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
  child.stdout?.on("data", chunk => { stdout += chunk; });
  register(child);
  child.stdin?.on("error", () => {});
  let error: Error | undefined;
  let actualPid = child.pid;
  let actualCode: number | null = null;
  let actualSignal: NodeJS.Signals | null = null;
  let startedResolve!: () => void, startedReject!: (error: Error) => void, startedSettled = false;
  const started = new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => { startedResolve = resolve; startedReject = reject; });
  void started.catch(() => {}); // command() observes close/error instead; host startup awaits this promise.
  const didStart = () => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedResolve(); } };
  const failedStart = (value: unknown) => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedReject(value instanceof Error ? value : Error(String(value))); } };
  if (!grouped) didStart();
  child.on("message", message => {
    const event = message as {type?:string;pid?:number;code?:number|null;signal?:NodeJS.Signals|null;error?:string};
    if (event.type === "started" && typeof event.pid === "number") { actualPid = event.pid; didStart(); }
    if (event.type === "result") { actualCode = event.code ?? null; actualSignal = event.signal ?? null; if (event.error) error = Error(event.error); }
  });
  child.on("error", value => { error = value; failedStart(value); });
  const closed = new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => child.once("close", () => {
    failedStart(error ?? Error("proof command exited before its process-group handshake"));
    groupGone(child).then(resolve,reject);
  }));
  // Hosts use stopChild() as their cleanup join; commands await closed directly.
  // Observe the promise here as well so an early frontend close cannot create
  // an unhandled rejection before its startup catch reaches stopChild().
  void closed.catch(() => {});
  return { child, logs, id, closed, started, pid: () => actualPid, code: () => grouped ? actualCode : child.exitCode, signal: () => grouped ? actualSignal : child.signalCode, stdout: () => options.secret ? stdout : logText(logs.stdout), error: () => error };
}
export const logText = (path: string): string => readFileSync(path, "utf8");
export async function ready(run: ReturnType<typeof logged>, parse: (line: string) => string | undefined, timeoutMs: number): Promise<string> {
  const end = performance.now() + timeoutMs;
  let outAt = 0, errAt = 0;
  while (performance.now() < end) {
    if (run.error()) throw run.error();
    if (run.child.exitCode !== null || run.child.signalCode !== null) {
      throw Error(`proof child exited before ready (${run.child.exitCode ?? run.child.signalCode}); ${run.logs.stderr}\n${logText(run.logs.stderr).slice(-4000)}`);
    }
    for (const [path, offset, stream] of [[run.logs.stdout, outAt, "out"], [run.logs.stderr, errAt, "err"]] as const) {
      const text = logText(path);
      const complete = text.lastIndexOf("\n") + 1;
      for (const line of text.slice(offset, complete).split("\n")) {
        const url = parse(stripVTControlCharacters(line).trim());
        if (url) return url;
      }
      if (stream === "out") outAt = complete; else errAt = complete;
    }
    await sleep(25);
  }
  throw Error(`proof child ready timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms; logs: ${run.logs.stdout}, ${run.logs.stderr}`);
}

/** Read every page by passing each opaque `next` back unchanged. The callback
 * receives null first. Refusals, loading, malformed/repeated cursors and a
 * capped or incomplete page fail instead of returning a partial snapshot. */
/** @throws E_PROOF_PAGE for a refused, loading, malformed, repeated, incomplete or over-limit traversal; callback errors propagate. */
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — proof traversal must never promote capped or partial reads to complete evidence.
export async function exhaustPages<Row>(readPage: (cursor: Cursor | null) => Promise<ProofPage<Row>>, options: ExhaustPagesOptions = {}): Promise<Row[]> {
  const maxPages = options.maxPages ?? 1_000, label = options.label ?? "paged read";
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(maxPages) || maxPages < 1) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: maxPages must be a positive safe integer`);
  const rows: Row[] = [], seen = new Set<string>();
  let cursor: Cursor | null = null;
  for (let pageNumber = 1; pageNumber <= maxPages; pageNumber++) {
    const page = await readPage(cursor);
    if (!page || typeof page !== "object") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned no read envelope`);
    if ("denied" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} refused ${page.denied.code}: ${page.denied.message}`);
    if ("loading" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is still loading`);
    if (!Array.isArray(page.data)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} data is not an array`);
    if (page.cut !== null) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (${page.cut === undefined ? "missing" : page.cut} cut)`);
    if (page.complete !== true) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (complete must be true)`);
    if (page.existence === "partial") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} has partial existence`);
    rows.push(...page.data);
    const next = page.next ?? null;
    if (next === null) return rows;
    if (typeof next !== "string" || next.length === 0) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a malformed cursor`);
    if (seen.has(next)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a repeated cursor`);
    seen.add(next);
    cursor = next as Cursor;
  }
  throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: exceeded maxPages ${maxPages}`);
}

//! @ref LLP 3000.000.000.000#11-old-client-operation-contracts-rel5 — compare old callers with the candidate, separately from data adoption.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — declared table renames preserve Ref inputs; additive result fields are notes.
use crate::{Bound, BoundProgram, types::Ty};
use snapback4_core::ir::{ArgType as A, ProgramKind};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

/// Conservative input-domain inclusion: every value accepted by old is accepted by new.
pub fn accepts(old: &A, new: &A) -> bool {
    accepts_in(old,new,None,None)
}

fn accepts_in(old: &A, new: &A, old_bound: Option<&Bound>, new_bound: Option<&Bound>) -> bool {
    if old==new {return true;}
    match (old,new) {
        (A::Optional(a),A::Optional(b))=>accepts_in(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
        (A::Optional(_),_)=>false,
        (a,A::Optional(b))=>accepts_in(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
        (A::Ref{table:old},A::Ref{table:new})=>new_bound.is_some_and(|bound|bound.schema.table_renames.get(new)==Some(old))
            && old_bound.is_some_and(|bound|bound.schema.table(old).is_some()),
        (A::Text{min:a,max:b,format:af},A::Text{min:c,max:d,format:bf})=>c<=a && d>=b && (bf.is_none() || af==bf),
        (A::IntRange{..},A::Int)=>true,
        (A::IntRange{min:a,max:b},A::IntRange{min:c,max:d})=>c<=a && d>=b,
        (A::Enum{variants:a},A::Enum{variants:b})=>a.iter().all(|v|b.contains(v)),
        (A::Bytes{max:a},A::Bytes{max:b}) | (A::Image{max:a},A::Image{max:b}) |
        (A::Video{max:a},A::Video{max:b})=>b>=a,
        (A::Json{max_bytes:a},A::Json{max_bytes:b})=>b>=a,
        (A::File{max:a,types:at},A::File{max:b,types:bt})=>b>=a && snapback4_core::assets::FILE_TYPES.iter().all(|t|!snapback4_core::assets::file_accepts(at,t)||snapback4_core::assets::file_accepts(bt,t)),
        (A::List{..}|A::ListRange{..},A::List{..}|A::ListRange{..})=> {
            let parts=|t:&A|match t {A::List{of,max}=>(0,*max,of.clone()),A::ListRange{of,min,max}=>(*min,*max,of.clone()),_=>unreachable!()};
            let (a,b,at)=parts(old);let(c,d,bt)=parts(new);
            c<=a && d>=b && match(at,bt){(_,None)=>true,(Some(a),Some(b))=>accepts_in(&a,&b,old_bound,new_bound),_=>false}
        }
        _=>false,
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ResultChange { Same, Additive, Changed }

fn combine(fields: impl IntoIterator<Item=ResultChange>, extra: bool) -> ResultChange {
    let mut additive=extra;
    for field in fields {
        match field {ResultChange::Changed=>return ResultChange::Changed,ResultChange::Additive=>additive=true,ResultChange::Same=>{}}
    }
    if additive {ResultChange::Additive} else {ResultChange::Same}
}

fn table_fields(name: &str, bound: &Bound) -> Option<BTreeMap<String,String>> {
    let schema=bound.schema.public_projection();
    let table=schema.tables.get(name)?;
    Some(table.columns.iter().filter(|(n,_)|!table.engine_field(n)).map(|(n,t)|(n.clone(),format!("{t:?};private={};constraints={:?}",table.read_optional(n),table.constraints.iter().filter(|c|matches!(c,snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Text{field,..} if field==n)).collect::<Vec<_>>()))).collect())
}

fn map_change<T>(old: &BTreeMap<String,T>, new: &BTreeMap<String,T>, compare: impl Fn(&T,&T)->ResultChange) -> ResultChange {
    combine(old.iter().map(|(name,old)|new.get(name).map(|new|compare(old,new)).unwrap_or(ResultChange::Changed)),new.len()>old.len())
}

fn result_change(old: &Ty, new: &Ty, old_bound: &Bound, new_bound: &Bound) -> ResultChange {
    if result(old,old_bound)==result(new,new_bound) {return ResultChange::Same;}
    match (old,new) {
        (Ty::Optional(a),Ty::Optional(b))|(Ty::Omittable(a),Ty::Omittable(b))
        |(Ty::List(a,_),Ty::List(b,_))|(Ty::Collection(a,_),Ty::Collection(b,_))=>result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
        (Ty::Object(a)|Ty::RowShape(a)|Ty::RowObject(a),Ty::Object(b)|Ty::RowShape(b)|Ty::RowObject(b))=>map_change(a,b,|a,b|result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound)),
        (Ty::Row(a),Ty::Row(b)) | (Ty::WriteRow(a),Ty::WriteRow(b)) | (Ty::Page(a,_),Ty::Page(b,_)) if a==b=>{
            let (Some(a),Some(b))=(table_fields(a,old_bound),table_fields(b,new_bound)) else{return ResultChange::Changed;};
            combine(a.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if b.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),b.len()>a.len())
        }
        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
    }
}

fn action_result_change(old: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>, new: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>) -> ResultChange {
    match (old,new) {
        (None,None)=>ResultChange::Same,
        (Some(old),Some(new))=>combine(old.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if new.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),new.len()>old.len()),
        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
    }
}

pub fn is_note(line: &str) -> bool { line.contains(": RESULT NOTE:") }

fn result(ty: &Ty, bound: &Bound) -> String {
    match ty {
        Ty::Row(name)|Ty::WriteRow(name)|Ty::Page(name,_)=> {
            let schema=bound.schema.public_projection();
            if let Some(table)=schema.tables.get(name) {
                let fields: BTreeMap<_,_>=table.columns.iter().filter(|(n,_)|!table.engine_field(n)).map(|(n,t)|(n,format!("{t:?};private={};constraints={:?}",table.read_optional(n),table.constraints.iter().filter(|c|matches!(c,snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Text{field,..} if field==n)).collect::<Vec<_>>()))).collect();
                let kind=match ty {Ty::Row(..)=>"row",Ty::WriteRow(..)=>"write-row",Ty::Page(..)=>"page",_=>unreachable!()};
                format!("{kind}:{name}:{fields:?}")
            } else {format!("{ty:?}")}
        }
        Ty::Optional(t)=>format!("optional {}",result(t,bound)),
        Ty::Omittable(t)=>format!("omittable {}",result(t,bound)),
        Ty::List(t,_)|Ty::Collection(t,_)=>format!("list {}",result(t,bound)),
        Ty::Object(fields)|Ty::RowShape(fields)|Ty::RowObject(fields)=>format!("object {:?}",fields.iter().map(|(n,t)|(n,result(t,bound))).collect::<BTreeMap<_,_>>()),
        Ty::Text(max)=>format!("text<={max}"),
        _=>format!("{ty:?}"),
    }
}

fn refusals(p: &BoundProgram) -> Vec<String> {
    fn walk(v: &serde_json::Value, out: &mut Vec<String>) {
        match v {
            serde_json::Value::Object(o)=> {
                if let Some(r)=o.get("Require") {out.push(format!("{}:{}",r["code"],r["message"]));}
                for v in o.values(){walk(v,out);}
            }
            serde_json::Value::Array(a)=>for v in a{walk(v,out);},
            _=>{}
        }
    }
    let mut out=Vec::new();walk(&serde_json::to_value(&p.program.body).unwrap(),&mut out);out
}

/// Reports are advisory: compatibility cannot license calls or prove unchanged behavior.
pub fn compare(old: &Bound, new: &Bound, label: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut lines=Vec::new();
    for before in old.programs.iter().filter(|p|p.program.kind!=ProgramKind::Job) {
        let name=&before.program.name;
        let prefix=format!("old-client compatibility ({label}), operation {name}");
        let Some(after)=new.programs.iter().find(|p|p.program.name==*name) else {
            lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed operation; old calls get E_OP; keep `alias {name} = replacement` for a same-module query/mutation, or retain a wrapper"));continue;
        };
        if before.program.kind!=after.program.kind {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: operation kind changed; retain the old endpoint kind"));continue;}
        let rename_candidate = |new_kind: &A| before.program.args.iter().find(|(old_name, old_kind)|
            !after.program.args.contains_key(*old_name) && !after.program.arg_aliases.contains_key(*old_name)
                && accepts_in(old_kind,new_kind,Some(old),Some(new)));
        let mut warned_renames=BTreeSet::new();
        for (arg,kind) in &after.program.args {
            if before.program.args.contains_key(arg) { continue; }
            if let Some((old_arg,old_kind))=before.program.args.iter().find(|(old,_)|after.program.arg_aliases.get(*old)==Some(arg)) {
                if !accepts_in(old_kind,kind,Some(old),Some(new)) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: aliased argument {old_arg} → {arg} narrows the old input domain ({old_kind:?} → {kind:?}); retain the old input domain or a compatible wrapper"));}
            } else if !matches!(kind,A::Optional(_)) {
                if let Some((old,_))=rename_candidate(kind) {
                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: required argument {old} appears renamed to {arg}; old calls get E_INPUT; declare `{arg}: <new type> alias {old}` if it is the same value, or retain a compatible wrapper"));
                    warned_renames.insert(old.clone());
                } else {
                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: clients calling without new required argument {arg} get E_INPUT; give {arg} a fitting `default <literal>` or retain a compatible wrapper"));
                }
            }
        }
        for (arg,kind) in &before.program.args {
            match after.program.args.get(arg) {
                None if after.program.arg_aliases.contains_key(arg)=>{
                    let next=&after.program.args[&after.program.arg_aliases[arg]];
                    if !accepts_in(kind,next,Some(old),Some(new)){lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: aliased argument {arg} retyped or narrowed ({kind:?} → {next:?}); retain its old input domain"));}
                },
                None if warned_renames.contains(arg)=>{},
                None=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed argument {arg}; old calls sending it get E_INPUT; retain `{arg}: <old type> deprecated` on a query/mutation")),
                Some(next) if !accepts_in(kind,next,Some(old),Some(new))=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: argument {arg} retyped or narrowed ({kind:?} → {next:?}); old values may get E_INPUT; retain the old input domain or a compatible wrapper")),
                _=>{}
            }
        }
        for (alias,canonical) in &before.program.arg_aliases {
            let old_kind=&before.program.args[canonical];
            let next=after.program.args.get(alias).or_else(||after.program.arg_aliases.get(alias).and_then(|name|after.program.args.get(name)));
            match next {
                None=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed argument alias {alias}; old calls sending it get E_INPUT; retain its alias or a compatible wrapper")),
                Some(kind) if !accepts_in(old_kind,kind,Some(old),Some(new))=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: argument alias {alias} retyped or narrowed ({old_kind:?} → {kind:?}); retain its old input domain")),
                _=>{}
            }
        }
        let mut positions:BTreeMap<String,String>=BTreeMap::new();
        for canonical in before.program.args.keys() {
            for spelling in std::iter::once(canonical).chain(before.program.arg_aliases.iter().filter_map(|(alias,target)|(target==canonical).then_some(alias))) {
                let target=after.program.args.contains_key(spelling).then_some(spelling).or_else(||after.program.arg_aliases.get(spelling));
                if let Some(target)=target {
                    if let Some(prior)=positions.insert(target.clone(),canonical.clone())&&prior!=*canonical {
                        lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: independent arguments {prior} and {canonical} now share {target}; old calls containing both positions get E_INPUT; retain separate arguments or a compatible wrapper"));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        for (table,before_table) in old.schema.visible_tables() {
            let Some(after_table)=new.schema.table(table) else { continue; };
            if !snapback4_core::ir::read_sites(&before.program).iter().any(|site|site.table==*table)
                && !snapback4_core::ir::write_tables(&before.program).iter().any(|(name,_)|name==table) { continue; }
            for field in before_table.columns.keys().filter(|f|!before_table.read_optional(f)&&after_table.read_optional(f)) {
                lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: {table}.{field} is now audience-optional; handle an omitted row property or a null explicit scalar before adopting the new column read rule"));
            }
        }
        let action_change=action_result_change(old.schema.action_specs.get(name).and_then(|s|s.returns.as_ref()),new.schema.action_specs.get(name).and_then(|s|s.returns.as_ref()));
        let typed_change=result_change(&before.result,&after.result,old,new);
        let change=combine([action_change,typed_change],false);
        match change {
            ResultChange::Additive=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT NOTE: result shape added fields while preserving prior fields and domains; old clients may ignore the additions")),
            ResultChange::Changed=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: result shape/value domain changed; preserve the old projection/domain or introduce a new operation before retiring old clients")),
            ResultChange::Same=>{},
        }
        let old_domains=crate::result_domains::signature(before,old);
        let new_domains=crate::result_domains::signature(after,new);
        // A domain introduced only for a newly returned field is covered by
        // the additive result note. Existing or removed domains still need review.
        let changed:Vec<_>=old_domains.keys().collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>().into_iter().filter(|key|old_domains.get(*key)!=new_domains.get(*key)).cloned().collect();
        if !changed.is_empty() {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: declared source domains consumed by this operation changed: {}; results or refusals may change even when the TypeScript type stays number/string; preserve the old domains or verify old-client handling",changed.join(", ")));}
        if refusals(before)!=refusals(after) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: BEHAVIOR REVIEW: refusal codes/messages changed ({:?} → {:?}); verify intended denials separately from input breaks",refusals(before),refusals(after)));}
    }
    lines
}

/// Human result advice groups source columns across operations. JSON keeps compare().
pub fn compact(lines:&[String])->Vec<String>{
    use std::collections::BTreeSet;
    let mut out=Vec::new();let mut groups=BTreeMap::<String,BTreeSet<String>>::new();
    for line in lines {
        let Some((prefix,detail))=line.split_once(": RESULT REVIEW: ") else {out.push(line.clone());continue};
        let operation=prefix.rsplit_once("operation ").map(|(_,name)|name).unwrap_or("unknown");
        if let Some((_,columns))=detail.split_once("declared source domains consumed by this operation changed: ") {
            for column in columns.split(';').next().unwrap_or(columns).split(", "){groups.entry(column.into()).or_default().insert(operation.into());}
        }else{groups.entry(detail.into()).or_default().insert(operation.into());}
    }
    for(detail,ops)in groups{out.push(format!("old-client compatibility: RESULT REVIEW: {detail}; operations [{}]; verify old-client handling (full per-operation evidence in --json)",ops.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")));}
    out
}

impl SavedVersion {
    pub(super) fn prepare(project: &Project, sources: &[(String,String)], bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound, options: &Options, deployment: &std::path::Path) -> Result<Option<Self>,String> {
        let Some(name) = options.flags.get("save-version") else {return Ok(None);};

            return Err("cannot save a version inside deployment custody; run deploy from the application's source directory".into());
        }
        let suffix = name.strip_prefix("versions/v").ok_or("--save-version needs a new project-relative versions/vN directory")?;
        if suffix.is_empty() || suffix.starts_with('0') || !suffix.bytes().all(|b|b.is_ascii_digit()) {return Err("--save-version needs versions/vN with a positive numeric N".into());}
        let parent=project.root.join("versions");
        if std::fs::symlink_metadata(&parent).is_ok_and(|m|m.file_type().is_symlink()) {return Err("--save-version refuses a symlinked versions directory".into());}
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&parent).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
        let path=project.root.join(name);
        let refresh = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(&path) {
            Ok(meta) if meta.file_type().is_symlink() || !meta.is_dir() => return Err(format!("cannot refresh {name}: saved version must be a real directory")),
            Ok(_) => {

                if existing != selected {return Err(format!("cannot refresh {name}: selected source differs from the saved source; choose a new versions/vN"));}
                true
            }

            Err(error) => return Err(format!("cannot inspect {name}: {error}")),
        };

        files.push((PathBuf::from("generated/api.ts"),snapback4_lang::emit::typescript(bound).into_bytes()));
        files.push((PathBuf::from("generated/package.json"),crate::project::GENERATED_PACKAGE.as_bytes().to_vec()));

                }
            }
        }

    }
    pub(super) fn finish(&mut self, release: u64, source_hash: &str) -> Result<(),String> {
        self.files.push((PathBuf::from("release.json"),format!("{}\n",serde_json::json!({"release":release,"sourceHash":source_hash,"cliVersion":env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")})).into_bytes()));
        for (name,bytes) in &self.files {
            let path=self.path.join(name);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if self.refresh {
                let temporary=path.with_extension(format!("refresh-{}",std::process::id()));
                std::fs::write(&temporary,bytes).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
                std::fs::rename(&temporary,&path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            } else {
                use std::io::Write;
                let mut file=std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).open(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
                file.write_all(bytes).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            }
        }
        self.complete=true;
        eprintln!("{} release {release} sources, generated client, contemporary fixtures and release.json at {}",if self.refresh {"refreshed"} else {"saved"},self.path.display());
        Ok(())
    }
}

pub(super) fn staging(shared: &Shared) -> Result<bool, snapback4_core::Refusal> {

fn clock_service(request: &Request, shared: &Shared) -> Result<Option<String>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — real-user dev clock authority is independent of fixture doors.
    if shared.personas {
        match super::session_identity::principal_of(request,shared) {
            Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind == "service" && principal == "service:operator" => return Ok(Some(principal)),
            _ if shared.dev_doors() && crate::auth::bearer_token(request).is_err() => return Ok(None),
            _ => return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "development clock control requires a full service:operator token").guide("clock")),
        }

        _ => Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "staging clock control requires a full service token").guide("clock")),
    }
}

}

pub(super) fn clock_status(request: Request, shared: &Shared) {
    if let Err(why) = clock_service(&request, shared) { return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&why)})); }
    let result = (|| {
        let (epoch, reader) = shared.reader()?;
        let note = crate::dev_clock_store::ahead(&reader, shared.now());
        lock(&shared.readers).put(&epoch, reader.into_inner());
        note
    })();
    match result {
        Ok(note) => { let now = shared.now(); respond(request, 200, json!({"storeAhead":note,"now":now,"skewMs":now - snapback4_core::now_ms()})) },
        Err(error) => respond(request, refusal_status(&error.refusal(), 500), json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
    }
}

//! Release activation extends the existing engine transaction and generation.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#5-hot-activation-and-ownership — CAS includes every activation, not only semantic changes.
use super::*;

#[derive(Clone,Debug,serde::Serialize,serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct HiddenNull {pub table:String,pub column:String,pub reason:String}
#[derive(Clone,Debug,serde::Serialize,serde::Deserialize,Default)]
pub struct VisibilityPolicy {pub hides:Vec<HiddenNull>}
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ReleaseActivation {
    pub visibility:Option<VisibilityPolicy>,
    pub release: u64,
    pub expected_previous: Option<u64>,
    pub expected_revision: Option<u64>,
    pub restore_dormant: bool,
    pub native_digest: Option<String>,
    pub operation: String,
}
pub(crate) trait ReleaseTransaction {
    fn selected_release(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn release_revision(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
}

impl ReleaseActivation {
    pub fn new(release: u64, expected_previous: Option<u64>) -> Self {
        Self {
            visibility:None,
            release,
            expected_previous,
            expected_revision: None,
            restore_dormant: true,
            native_digest: None,
            operation: "activate".into(),
        }
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.009.001.000#9.1 — validate new text keys before opening an activation writer.
    pub(crate) fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if self.operation.contains('\0') || self.native_digest.as_deref().is_some_and(|s| s.contains('\0')) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Input("release operation and native digest cannot contain U+0000".into()));
        }
        crate::release_history::counter(self.release)?;
        self.expected_previous.map(crate::release_history::counter).transpose()?;
        self.expected_revision.map(crate::release_history::counter).transpose()?;
        Ok(())
    }
    pub(crate) fn check(&self, tx: &impl ReleaseTransaction) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.validate()?;
        let actual = tx.selected_release()?;
        if actual
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok() != self.expected_previous)
        {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("current release changed; run `snapback4 releases <dir>` and retry the selected release".into()));
        }
        let revision = tx.release_revision()?;
        let revision = revision.and_then(|v| v.parse::<u64>().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
        if self.expected_revision.is_some_and(|n| n != revision) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("activation revision changed (including rollback/equal-content activation); run `snapback4 releases <dir>` and retry".into()));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Engine {
    pub fn new_release(
        store: impl Into<AnyStore>,
        schema: Schema,
        programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
        release: u64,
        expected_previous: Option<u64>,
    ) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
        Self::new_release_with_feed_adoption(
            store,
            schema,
            programs,
            release,
            expected_previous,
            false,
        )
    }
    pub fn new_release_with_feed_adoption(
        store: impl Into<AnyStore>,
        schema: Schema,
        programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
        release: u64,
        expected_previous: Option<u64>,
        allow_feed_adoption: bool,
    ) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
        Self::new_release_prepared(
            store,
            schema,
            programs,
            &ReleaseActivation::new(release, expected_previous),
            allow_feed_adoption,
        )
    }
    pub fn new_release_prepared(
        store: impl Into<AnyStore>, schema: Schema, programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
        options: &ReleaseActivation, allow_feed_adoption: bool,
    ) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
        Self::new_release_prepared_at(store,schema,programs,options,allow_feed_adoption,crate::now_ms())
    }
    pub fn new_release_prepared_at(
        store: impl Into<AnyStore>,
        mut schema: Schema,
        programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
        options: &ReleaseActivation,
        allow_feed_adoption: bool,
        now: i64,
    ) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
        let mut store = store.into();
        prepare(&mut schema)?;
        let programs = programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p)).collect();
        let (generation, metadata) = Self::activate(
            &mut store,
            &schema,
            &programs,
            Some(options),
            now,
            allow_feed_adoption,
            None,
            None,
        )?.into_inner();
        store.exclude_ephemeral(&schema);
        Ok(Self {
            timeline_schedule: timeline::Schedule::default(),
            ephemeral: std::sync::Arc::new(ephemeral::Hub::new(
                metadata.store_id,
                generation,
                &schema,
            )),
            store,
            schema,
            programs,
            generation,
            expiry_after: BTreeMap::new(),
            dev_effects: false,
            ceilings: Ceilings::default(),
            entropy: crate::ids::seed(),
            minter: crate::ids::Mint::default(),
            #[cfg(feature = "native")]
            native: None,
            #[cfg(feature = "native")]
            native_logs: native::Logs::default(),
            presence: None,
        })
    }
    /// No replacement engine, post-commit SQL read, or fallible ephemeral swap.
    pub fn adopt_release(
        &mut self, schema: Schema, programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
        options: &ReleaseActivation, allow_feed_adoption: bool,
    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.adopt_release_at(schema,programs,options,allow_feed_adoption,crate::now_ms())
    }
    pub fn adopt_release_at(
        &mut self,
        mut schema: Schema,
        programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
        options: &ReleaseActivation,
        allow_feed_adoption: bool,
        now: i64,
    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        let programs = programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p)).collect();
        prepare(&mut schema)?;
        super::activation_facts::check_operations(&self.schema, &schema, &self.programs, &programs)?;
        drop(self.ephemeral.lock()?);
        Ok(Committer::run_committed_with(self, |engine| {
            Self::activate(
            &mut engine.store,
            &schema,
            &programs,
            Some(options),
            now,
            allow_feed_adoption,
            None,
            None,
            ).map(|committed| committed.pending((schema, programs)))
        }, |engine, (schema, programs), (generation, metadata)| {
            engine.store.exclude_ephemeral(&schema);
            engine.timeline_schedule = timeline::Schedule::default();
            engine.schema = schema;
            engine.programs = programs;
            engine.generation = generation;
            engine.expiry_after.clear();
            engine.dev_effects = false;
            engine.ephemeral
                .rebind_committed(metadata.store_id, generation, &engine.schema);
            Ok(generation)
        })?.into_inner())
    }
    #[cfg(feature = "native")]
    pub fn set_prepared_native(&mut self, module: Option<std::sync::Arc<native::Module>>) {
        self.native = module;
    }
}
